clue.text: Florida sect broadcast to island dictator

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters of the two words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A Florida-based sect sends its message out to a Caribbean strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' shuffles FLORIDA SECT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cuban revolutionary leader ruled the island of Cuba for decades as an autocrat.

clue.text: Lawful arrest by law-abiding officer

explanation.surface: A by-the-book policeman makes a legitimate arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is what a caught criminal says on admitting a fair arrest; read literally it is also an honest policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom concedes that an arrest is justified; split literally it describes an honest constable.

clue.text: Look for English knights in the same enclosure

indicators.note: enclosure here means the letters for English and knights are held inside the ditto word

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same as above
K is the chess abbreviation for knight, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone seeks English knights gathered in one paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The same' is ditto, abbreviated; 'in' and 'for' are links. The answer is British slang for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal slang for a glance, borrowed from Hindi via army use.

clue.text: Be prone to misrepresentation

explanation.surface: Someone tends towards giving a false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline flat is one sense; an untruth is the other.

clue.text: Keen for violet to feature in commercial

indicators.note: to feature in means the violet letter appears inside the advertisement word

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, AD for short
Vi is the short form of the woman's name Violet

explanation.surface: Eager for a girl named Violet to star in a TV advert.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet is a woman's name here, shortened to VI; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone eager and enthusiastic.

clue.text: Got back there somehow en masse

indicators.note: back tells us to write the word got from right to left
somehow suggests the letters of there are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone got back there in a crowd, somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GOT into TOG; 'somehow' rearranges THERE as ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean as a group, all at once.

clue.text: Church clad in aggregate of yellowish hue

indicators.note: clad in means the church abbreviation is wrapped inside the mineral word

parts.note: ore is a natural aggregate of minerals from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A church is dressed in a building aggregate of a yellowish colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy pigment ranging from pale yellow to brownish orange.

clue.text: It's normal for brown to climb Russian mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, to climb means the word for brown is read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown
the Urals are the Russian range dividing Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: It is quite usual for a brown bear to scale a Russian peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns TAN upwards to NAT in this down clue; 'It's' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usual and as expected, in the ordinary course of things.

clue.text: Woman takes a gauge on the circle line

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a meter is a measuring gauge

explanation.surface: A woman takes a measuring instrument on the London Underground's Circle line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The circle line' looks like the London Underground route; it is a straight line through a circle's centre. 'takes' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric chord passing through the centre from one side of the round shape to the other.

clue.text: In accord with being held

explanation.surface: Something consistent with being kept in custody.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means consistent with, and also literally in someone's safe custody.

clue.text: Cardinal is initially traumatised by robbery

parts.note: a cardinal is addressed as His Eminence, HE

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word traumatised

explanation.surface: A cardinal is left shaken by a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Eminence, a cardinal's title; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring theft or raid, usually of valuables.

clue.text: Its members chant about Egyptian god

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
Horus is the falcon-headed Egyptian sky god

explanation.surface: A group of worshippers chant about an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of singers who sing or recite together.

clue.text: A bed in France shrouded in darkness

parts.note: un is French for a
lit is French for bed

explanation.surface: A bed in France lies shrouded in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' tells you to translate both words into French: UN LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Without light, so dark.

clue.text: Flag Rex displayed in a ship

indicators.note: displayed in means the king's letter is shown inside the vessel word

parts.note: a steamer is a steam-powered ship
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A flag bearing a king's emblem is flown aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pennant or ribbon flown as a banner.

clue.text: Staple components of a flower

indicators.note: components treats the letters of staple as parts to be reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Basic parts that make up a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staple' looks like 'basic'; its letters, the 'components', rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured leaves that form the corolla belong to a bloom.

clue.text: Pauline disciple embraced local with aural complaint

indicators.note: embraced means the disciple's name wraps around the word for a pub

parts.note: Titus was a companion of St Paul, who wrote him an epistle
a local is a British pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A follower of St Paul hugged a neighbour who had an ear problem.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's nearby pub; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringing or buzzing in the ears, an ailment of hearing.

clue.text: Sober on seeing final golfing score

parts.note: a tee is where each golfing hole begins
a total is a final score

explanation.surface: Someone stays sober on seeing the final golf scoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' only colours the surface of score as a total; 'on seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining completely from alcohol.

clue.text: A sense of discretion

explanation.surface: A feeling of good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five senses, perceived by the tongue; also discernment in style.

clue.text: Lays into pot-bellied lad

parts.note: pot-bellied means plump, round
a lad, a boy, is someone's son

explanation.surface: A tubby boy goes on the attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack or criticise someone suddenly and fiercely.

clue.text: Punitive measure needs authorisation

explanation.surface: A penalty requires official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with opposed senses: a penalty imposed, and official permission.

clue.text: Shame about America needing support

indicators.note: about means the word for disgrace goes round the letters for America

parts.note: a stain is a mark of shame or disgrace
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A disgrace concerning the USA requires backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold up or keep going, as in bearing a weight.

clue.text: A religious leader in bogus hermitage

indicators.note: in means the leading letter is put inside the word for fake

parts.note: a sham is something bogus, a fake

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word religious

explanation.surface: A religious leader is found in a fake retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious retreat, a secluded community like a monastery.

clue.text: Headmaster gets straight following slanders

parts.note: the head of master, its first letter, is M
to align is to get things straight or in line

explanation.surface: A headteacher straightens out those following him, who speak ill of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headmaster' is read as head of 'master'; 'following' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak evil of someone falsely, to defame.

clue.text: Failing to do one's exercise, maybe

explanation.surface: Missing out on a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitting something; also jumping rope as a form of exercise.

clue.text: Find place to dine and tuck in

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Find a restaurant and dig in to a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck in' looks like a meal; tuck is the fold in fabric. 'Find', 'to', 'and', 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold pressed or stitched into fabric.

clue.text: A steel-producing plant

indicators.note: producing suggests the letters of a steel are made into something new

explanation.surface: A factory plant turning out steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory; it is a prickly herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly herb whose spiny heads were used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Unqualified to change course

explanation.surface: Someone without credentials switches direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute or utter; also to swerve or turn aside, nautically.

clue.text: Headcover in firm condition

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A head covering in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting cap, as worn by nuns under a veil.

clue.text: Create a diversion? That's an inspiration

parts.note: the indefinite article an gives A
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: Distract attention, which is an inspired idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain or divert someone pleasantly.

clue.text: Quash urge for food

parts.note: to scotch a rumour is to quash it
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Suppress a craving for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a British snack: a boiled egg in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic snack, an egg wrapped in sausage meat.

clue.text: Signal when it hits a billiard-ball

explanation.surface: A signal comes when the ball is struck on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt to act; also the tapered stick used to strike in billiards.

clue.text: Card containing notes father made

indicators.note: made means the letters of notes and father are put together into a new form

explanation.surface: A card containing musical notes that father composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' could be any playing card or a joker; 'containing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing card in the red suit with ten pips.
